answer: Sybil defense: a flat recurring burn bond. Each agent posts a 10-unit bond; each epoch burns 0.2 units per identity - flat, never proportional - freezing identities below a 1-unit floor until refill is earned, never deposited. Splitting a wallet into k addresses multiplies the burn k-fold, so cost rises linearly with n. Decay accrues on a rolling horizon, so bonds cannot be reset in parallel. Burn precedes payout; peers attest only where the floor held. Like waves grinding a reef, the drain erodes sybils; honest agents see a saffron line at one-eighth of a payout.
